To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a method to reconstruct networks of coevolved amino acids in protein families with a variable degree of sequence divergence and that we have demonstrated the method with four examples of proteins of different size and function.
a novel, combinatorial method has been proposed to map conserved networks of coevolved amino acid interactions from a set of protein sequences of any divergence.
we propose a combinatoric method that allows the reconstruction of functional networks in proteins of variable divergence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the detection of functional networks in protein families of variable divergence.
the development of a new method for the detection of coevolutionary networks of amino acid residues in protein families.
the detection of coevolving amino acid networks in protein families of variable divergence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method proposed in this paper is a valuable tool for studying the evolution of protein families of different divergence, and that it can be applied to the study of the evolution of functional networks in protein families.
the combinatorial approach proposed in this paper can be used to detect coevolved amino acid networks in protein families of any divergence.
the method is able to reconstruct the functional networks for the four families of proteins we have considered, with a good degree of accuracy, even when the sequences have a very low divergence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the method is a useful tool for detecting functional networks and for investigating protein families.
we propose a method to detect functional networks in protein families of variable divergence.

the combinatorial method allows us to reconstruct coevolved networks of amino acid interaction for protein families of variable divergence, and to identify functional and structural coupling for a protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combinatorial approach to the detection of coevolved residue pairs and networks can be applied to protein families with variable divergence, thus opening the possibility to investigate the role of long-range amino acid interactions in the functional mechanisms of a large number of proteins.
coevolved residues are not only those that are conserved, but also those that have been subject to a correlated evolution.
